title: Bengaluru Premium Homebuyer's Guide
subtitle: A practical companion for choosing, evaluating and buying a premium home in Bengaluru
intro: Buying a premium home is a sequence of decisions rather than a single one. This guide sets them out in a sensible order, from choosing a location to planning your next steps, and offers a checklist at each stage. It is written in general terms for buyers in Bengaluru and is not a substitute for independent legal or financial advice.

chapters.title: Choosing the right location
chapters.bodyHtml:
Bengaluru has grown along several corridors at once, and each has its own character. North Bengaluru is shaped by the airport corridor and established pockets such as Hennur and Yelahanka. East Bengaluru is anchored by Whitefield and its technology parks, with newer growth towards Hoskote. The south and south-east, including Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout, Hosa Road and Electronic City, combine mature neighbourhoods with large planned communities.

Rather than ranking zones, map them against your own routine. List the journeys your household makes most often, decide how much social infrastructure you need from day one, and be honest about whether you prefer a compact, walkable setting or a spacious, low-density one. The longer you intend to stay, the more weight you can give to a location's direction of travel.

  • List your five most frequent weekly journeys and estimate them for each zone.
  • Visit shortlisted locations on a weekday morning, a weekday evening and a weekend.
  • Walk the surroundings rather than driving through.
  • Verify planned infrastructure against official sources, not marketing material.

chapters.title: Comparing layouts and configurations
chapters.bodyHtml:
Configuration describes the number of bedrooms and the general format of a home: an apartment in a tower, a low-rise villament with a private garden or terrace, a duplex or a penthouse. Each suits a different way of living. Villaments offer a house-like feel with shared amenities; tower apartments often offer views, efficiency and a wider choice of plans.

Study floor plans with a scale rule rather than by impression. Check usable room dimensions, the size and placement of windows, the depth of balconies and whether the plan wastes space in corridors. Trace which rooms face which direction and what each window looks onto. Cross-ventilation, a kitchen that can be vented and bedrooms that do not face a neighbour directly are details that matter every day.

  • Confirm the household needs of the next five to ten years, including work-from-home space.
  • Compare plans on usable room sizes, not only on total area.
  • Note orientation, views and privacy for the specific unit, not the show home.
  • Ask which specifications are committed and which are indicative.

chapters.title: Understanding areas and pricing components
chapters.bodyHtml:
Three area terms appear on brochures and cost sheets. Carpet area, as defined under RERA, is the net usable floor area inside the home, including internal partition walls but excluding external walls, service shafts and exclusive balconies or terraces. Built-up area adds the enclosing walls and attached exclusive spaces. Super built-up area adds a proportionate share of common areas such as lobbies, corridors and the clubhouse.

Prices are often quoted per square foot on super built-up area, so the fairest comparison between homes is made by dividing the all-in price by the carpet area. The headline price is also only one component of the total outlay: statutory duties and taxes, parking, club and utility charges, deposits and interiors should all be in your budget.

  • Ask for RERA carpet area, exclusive balcony area and super built-up area for each unit.
  • Request a complete itemised cost sheet from every developer.
  • Compare projects on an all-in price per square foot of carpet area.
  • Budget separately for stamp duty, registration, applicable taxes and interiors.

chapters.title: Evaluating a developer and project
chapters.bodyHtml:
A project is a promise, and a developer's completed work is the best evidence of how promises are kept. Visit at least one delivered development by the same developer. Look at how the facade and landscape have aged, whether the amenities exist and are used, and speak to residents about handover and responsiveness.

Then study the master plan of the project itself. It shows how much land is left open, how dense the community is, how blocks are oriented to sun and breeze, how vehicles and people are separated, and where services such as treatment plants and generators sit. Read the specification sheet line by line against the show home.

  • Visit a completed project by the developer and talk to residents.
  • Assess open space, density, orientation and movement on the master plan.
  • Identify which homes are nearest to service installations.
  • Compare the specification sheet with what is installed in the show home.

chapters.title: Documents and RERA checks
chapters.bodyHtml:
The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act requires projects above a statutory size threshold to be registered with the state authority before they are marketed. Confirm the registration on the official Karnataka RERA portal and compare the registered promoter, approved plans and declared completion date with what you have been told.

Beyond RERA, the land documents establish what you are buying. These include the chain of title, the encumbrance certificate, municipal records, any land conversion order and, where the developer is building on someone else's land, the joint development agreement. Project documents include the sanctioned plan, commencement certificate and applicable clearances. Engage a lawyer experienced in Karnataka property transactions to review them.

  • Verify the RERA registration independently on the official portal.
  • Review title, encumbrance, khata and conversion documents with a lawyer.
  • Confirm the marketed project matches the sanctioned plan.
  • Read the draft agreement for sale in full before booking.

chapters.title: Payment plans and home loans
chapters.bodyHtml:
Most under-construction purchases follow a construction-linked plan, in which instalments fall due as the project reaches defined stages such as foundation, successive slabs, finishing and handover. Milestones should be objective and verifiable. Some developers also offer alternative structures; whatever the plan, make sure it is clearly written into the agreement.

If you intend to borrow, obtain a pre-approval early. It clarifies your ceiling, shortens the time to booking and signals seriousness. Lenders assess your income, obligations and credit history, and separately evaluate the project's legal and technical standing before disbursing against milestones. Terms vary by lender, so compare more than one.

  • Obtain a loan pre-approval before shortlisting in earnest.
  • Check that payment milestones are tied to verifiable construction stages.
  • Understand what happens on delay, cancellation or variation in carpet area.
  • Keep a reserve for costs that fall outside the loan, such as duties and interiors.

chapters.title: The site-visit checklist
chapters.bodyHtml:
A site visit is more than a tour of the show home. Bring your priority list and specific questions, and ask to see the actual position of the unit you are considering. Note orientation, views, distance to lifts and the location of service areas. If the project is under construction, ask to see the current stage of work alongside the sample home.

  • Approach roads: width, condition and alternative routes at peak times.
  • Surroundings: noise, light, neighbouring land use and future construction.
  • Master plan on the ground: open space, pedestrian routes, vehicle separation.
  • The specific unit: orientation, view, privacy, balcony depth, natural light.
  • Specifications: flooring, doors, windows, kitchen, bathrooms, electrical and security.
  • Services: water supply and storage, rainwater harvesting, power backup, connectivity.
  • Construction stage and quality where visible.
  • Questions on maintenance, association formation and handover process.

chapters.title: Planning your next steps
chapters.bodyHtml:
With the groundwork done, the path to a decision becomes clearer. Organise what you have learned under location, layout, pricing, developer, documents and finance. Note the questions that remain and put them to the developer in writing; the quality of the answers is itself informative.

When you are ready, ask for a complete cost sheet for the specific unit, the draft agreement for sale and the payment schedule. Have your lawyer review them, confirm your financing, and only then book. After booking, keep an organised file of every document and piece of correspondence through to registration and handover.

  • Shortlist two or three homes and compare them on an all-in basis.
  • Resolve open questions in writing before booking.
  • Complete legal review and financing before committing.
  • Keep a single organised record from booking to possession.

disclaimer: This guide is provided for general information only and does not constitute legal, financial or investment advice. Regulations, charges and procedures change from time to time and may vary by project and by buyer. Please verify all details with the relevant authorities and with qualified professional advisers before making any decision. Nothing in this guide is an offer or a representation regarding any specific development.
